public.title: Edit Distance
public.description: Two labels source and target contain only lowercase English letters, with each length from 0 through 120. Return the fewest single-character edits that turn source into target. One edit inserts one letter at any position, deletes one letter, or replaces one letter with another; each costs one. Exchanging adjacent letters is not a single edit. Return only the minimum cost, so no edit-script tie rule is needed. Empty strings are valid. Aim for O(m times n) time for lengths m and n.
hints: Compare prefixes of the two labels; remember the answer for each pair of prefix lengths.
When the final letters differ, consider an insertion, deletion or replacement. Only the preceding row and current row are needed.
public.attribution: Original statement, examples, tests and solutions authored for Bekor, 2026. Uses a standard algorithmic pattern; no third-party exercise text or code used.

explanation: Let dp(i,j) be the minimum cost for the first i source letters and first j target letters. Empty-prefix costs are i and j. Equal final letters extend the diagonal answer for free; otherwise take one plus the minimum of the deletion, insertion and replacement predecessors. Keep one previous row and build the next row. For lengths m and n, time is O(m times n + m + n) including empty inputs; auxiliary space is O(n + 1).
